newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes firmer on oversold signals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes firmer on oversold signals.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on signals the market was oversold, traders said.
Also, there were ideas the market may have found its seasonal bottom after the recent fall to contract lows and three-year lows, they said.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the July Tuesday closed at 19.8 percent and had recovered Wednesday to close at 24 percent. An RSI of 30 or less is viewed as an oversold market.
Analysts said harvesting continued to limit gains.
"Weather is pretty good and they're cutting in the St. Louis soft red winter area and the talk is of excellent, excellent yields," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst for E.D. and F. Man Interntional.
Sernatinger and others said the Kansas hard red winter wheat harvesting was progressing smoothly.
"There are awesome, awesome yields in northern Kansas. They may have a record Kansas crop," Sernatinger said.
CBOT soft red winter wheat closed one to three cents per bushel higher, with July up 1-1/2 at $3.24 per bushel. September was up one at $3.32-1/2.
In wheat options, Tenco Inc sold 400 December $3.70 calls at 9-1/4 cents and E.D. and F. Man Interntional bought 200 December $3.70 calls at 9-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 15,000 contracts, below the 17,136 traded Tuesday.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, slightly above the 4,828 traded Tuesday.
